exposure: monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancies complicated by twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS)
Perinatal survival of at least one twin (89.1% vs. 71.8%)
Gestational age at birth (32+3 vs. 29+1 weeks+days)
Perinatal survival of both twins (65.2% vs. 38.5%)
Traditional management (amniodrainage and/or emergency preterm cesarean delivery)
cohort: 46 monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancies complicated by twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome (TTTS) after 26 weeks gestation treated with fetoscopic laser surgery, compared with 39 cases managed with traditional management
finding: Fetoscopic laser surgery for MCDA twins complicated with TTTS between 26 and 31 weeks gestation is associated with a higher gestational age at birth and better perinatal survival than traditional management.
mod_finding: This study found that fetoscopic laser surgery for TTTS after 26 weeks gestation was associated with a lower frequency of preterm delivery compared to traditional management with amniodrainage and/or emergency preterm cesarean delivery.
